chunks: From him, from his father, from Suleyman al-Ja'fari, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida, from his father (peace be upon them), who said:

A group of people were presented to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) during one of his military expeditions, so he said: 'Who are these people?' They said: 'Believers, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'And what has reached of your faith?' They said: 'Patience during affliction, and gratitude during prosperity, and contentment with the divine decree.'

So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Forbearing, knowledgeable. They are so close to the Prophets through their jurisprudence that if you are as you describe yourselves, do not build what you will not dwell in, and do not amass what you will not consume, and fear Allah, to whom you will be returned.'
ai.seo_question: What are the characteristics of true faith and the Prophet's advice on wealth in this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi underscores the profound spiritual maturity of believers, characterizing them as 'wise scholars' whose depth of understanding (fiqh) approaches that of the Prophets. The Prophet’s advice to avoid building what one does not inhabit and accumulating what one does not consume reflects the Shia emphasis on detachment from worldly excess (zuhd) while maintaining active faith. This narrative reinforces the concept that true piety is measured by contentment with divine decree (rida) rather than material accumulation.
